draft.title: Perimeter of composite figures
card: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a shape. Add the lengths of all its outside edges, and give the answer in units of length such as cm or m.
A rectangle with length \(l\) and width \(w\) has two sides of each length. Its perimeter is \(2l + 2w\).
A composite figure is made from simpler shapes joined together. Work out any missing side lengths first, using the sides you are given.
Example: an L-shape has outside sides 10, 6, 4, 3, 6 and 3 cm, going around. Add every outside edge: \(10 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 32\) cm. Edges inside the figure are not counted.
draft.remember: Find the missing sides, then add every outside edge once.

a.q: A rectangular garden bed is 7 m long and 3 m wide. What is its perimeter?
a.why: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so \(7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20\) m. Adding only one length and one width gives 10 m, which is only half the distance around.
a.clue: Count every side of the rectangle, not just two.

b.q: An L-shaped courtyard in Orange has outside sides 12 m, 5 m, 7 m, 3 m, 5 m and a last side of unknown length, going around. The last side is the one that completes the shape back to the start. What is the perimeter?
b.why: Picture the L as a 12 m by 8 m rectangle, with sides 12 and 8 meeting at one corner. Then the missing side is 8 m and \(12 + 5 + 7 + 3 + 5 + 8 = 40\) m. This does not match the sides given, so the shape must be read with care.
b.clue: Check that the sides match before adding.

problems.detail: Read as an L-shape (one rectangle of 12 by 8 with a 7 by 3 notch removed), the missing side is 8 m and the perimeter is 40 m, which is not among the options. The why itself gets 40 m, so the intended answer is missing.

With no diagram or turn directions, the sides 12, 5, 7, 3, 5 fit two valid L-shapes. The missing side can be 8 m (perimeter 40 m) or 2 m (perimeter 34 m), so the question is ambiguous. Only 34 m among the options can be defended. Add a diagram and make sure the correct total is an option.

proposal.title: Perimeter of composite figures
card: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a shape. Add the lengths of all its outside edges, and give the answer in units of length such as cm or m.
A rectangle with length \(l\) and width \(w\) has two sides of each length. Its perimeter is \(2l + 2w\).
A composite figure is made from simpler shapes joined together. Find any missing side first. In an L-shape, the two shorter sides that run one way add up to the long side opposite them.

Example: an L-shape is 10 cm along the bottom and 6 cm up the right. The top is 4 cm and the left is 3 cm. The missing sides are \(6 - 3 = 3\) cm and \(10 - 4 = 6\) cm, so the perimeter is \(10 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 32\) cm.
proposal.remember: Find the missing sides first, then add every outside edge once.

a.q: A rectangular garden bed is 7 m long and 3 m wide. What is its perimeter?
a.why: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so \(7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20\) m. Adding only one length and one width gives 10 m, which is only half the distance around.
a.clue: Count every side of the rectangle, not just two.

b.q: An L-shaped courtyard in Orange is 12 m along the bottom and 8 m up the right side. Its top edge is 5 m and its left side is 3 m. The other two sides are not labelled. What is its perimeter?
b.why: The missing vertical side is \(8 - 3 = 5\) m and the missing horizontal side is \(12 - 5 = 7\) m. Then \(12 + 8 + 5 + 5 + 7 + 3 = 40\) m. Adding only the four labelled sides gives 28 m, which leaves out two outside edges.
b.clue: Use the long sides to find the two unlabelled sides.
